q-183317.name: Question 2
q-183317.problem:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

$$
U=\{5,10,15,20,25,30,35\},
$$

find the truth set of $P(x)⇒Q(x)$ for the following predicates: 

- $P(x):$ $x$ is odd.

- $Q(x):$ $\sqrt{x}$ is integer.
q-183317.worked_solution:
Since $P(x)⇒Q(x)≡¬P(x)∨Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={T}_{¬P∨Q} \\  & ={T}_{¬P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- The truth set of $P(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{P}=\{5,15,25,35\}.
$$

As a result, the complement is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\overset{―}{T}}_{P} & =\overset{―}{\{5,15,25,35\}} \\  & =\{10,20,30\}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The truth set of $Q(x)$ is 

$$
{T}_{Q}=\{25\}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & =\{10,20,30\}\cup \{25\} \\  & =\{10,20,25,30\}.\end{aligned}
$$

U={5,10,15,20,25,30,35},

  • P(x): x is odd.

  • Q(x): x is integer.

a

b
{25}
c
{5,15,25,35}
d
{10,20,25,30}
e
{10,20,30}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since P(x)⇒Q(x)≡¬P(x)∨Q(x), the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

TP⇒Q=T¬P∨Q=T¬P∪TQ=T―P∪TQ

Now, we note the following:

  • The truth set of P(x) is TP={5,15,25,35}. As a result, the complement is T―P={5,15,25,35}―={10,20,30}.

  • The truth set of Q(x) is TQ={25}.

Therefore, we have

TP⇒Q=T―P∪TQ={10,20,30}∪{25}={10,20,25,30}.

q-183378.name: Question 4
q-183378.problem:
Find the truth set of $P(x)⇔Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $R:$

- $P(x):$ ${x}^{2}\le 9$

- $Q(x):$ $5x-3>7$
q-183378.worked_solution:
Since we have that

$$
P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),
$$

 

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇔Q}=({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- To find the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & \le 9 \\ -3 & \le x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is 
${T}_{P}=[-3,3].$ 
As a result, the complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=(-\infty ,-3)\cup (3,\infty ).$

- To find the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-3 & >7 \\ 5x & >10 \\ x & >2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is
${T}_{Q}=(2,\infty ),$
and its complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}=(-\infty ,2].$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q} & =[-3,3]\cap (2,\infty ) \\  & =(2,3] \\ {\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q} & =((-\infty ,-3)\cup (3,\infty ))\cap (-\infty ,2] \\  & =(-\infty ,-3) \\ {T}_{P⇔Q} & =({T}_{P}\cap {T}_{Q})\cup ({\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cap {\overset{―}{T}}_{Q}) \\  & =(2,3]\cup (-\infty ,-3) \\  & =(-\infty ,-3)\cup (2,3].\end{aligned}
$$

q-183378.html:
Question 4
?

Find the truth set of P(x)⇔Q(x) given the following predicates defined over the universal set R:

  • P(x): x2≤9

  • Q(x): 5x−3>7

a
(−∞,2)
b
 (2,∞)
c
 [−3,3]
d
 (−∞,−3)∪(2,3]
e
 (−2,∞)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since we have that

P(x)⇔Q(x)≡(P(x)∧Q(x))∨(¬P(x)∧¬Q(x)),

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

TP⇔Q=(TP∩TQ)∪(T―P∩T―Q)

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the truth set of P(x), we solve the inequality: x2≤9−3≤x≤3 So, the truth set of P(x) is TP=[−3,3]. As a result, the complement is T―P=(−∞,−3)∪(3,∞).
  • To find the truth set of Q(x), we solve the inequality: 5x−3>75x>10x>2 So, the truth set of Q(x) is TQ=(2,∞), and its complement is T―Q=(−∞,2].

Therefore, we have

TP∩TQ=[−3,3]∩(2,∞)=(2,3]T―P∩T―Q=((−∞,−3)∪(3,∞))∩(−∞,2]=(−∞,−3)TP⇔Q=(TP∩TQ)∪(T―P∩T―Q)=(2,3]∪(−∞,−3)=(−∞,−3)∪(2,3].

q-183356.name: Question 5
q-183356.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\,$ $A(x):$ $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N.$ $\,$ $B(x):$ $x\in \{3,7\}.$ 

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x)⇔B(x)?$

I. $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ is equivalent to  $x\in N.$

II. $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ if and only if $x\in \{3,7\}.$

III. If $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ then $x\in \{3,7\},$ or if $x\in \{3,7\}$ then $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N.$
q-183356.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A⇔B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ if and only if $x\in \{3,7\}.$

- $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ is equivalent to $x\in \{3,7\}.$

- If $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N$ then $x\in \{3,7\},$ and if $x\in \{3,7\}$ then $x\in \{-1,0,3,7\}\cap N.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Question 5
?

Consider the following predicates.

A(x): x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N. B(x): x∈{3,7}.

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate A(x)⇔B(x)?

  1. x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N is equivalent to x∈N.
  2. x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N if and only if x∈{3,7}.
  3. If x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N then x∈{3,7}, or if x∈{3,7} then x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N.
a
III only
b
I, II, and III
c
II only
d
I and II only
e
II and III only
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A biconditional expression P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P) can be read as shown below:

  • P if and only if Q

  • P is equivalent to Q

  • If P then Q, and if Q then P

So, A⇔B translates into the following sentences:

  • x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N if and only if x∈{3,7}.

  • x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N is equivalent to x∈{3,7}.

  • If x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N then x∈{3,7}, and if x∈{3,7} then x∈{−1,0,3,7}∩N.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

q-171781.name: Question 6
q-171781.problem:
Consider the following predicates.

$\,$ $P(x):$ $x\,|\,8.$ $\,$ $Q(x):$ $x$ is even.

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $P(x)⇔Q(x)?$

I. If $x\,|\,8$ then $x$ is even, or if $x$ is even then $x\,|\,8.$

II. If $x\,|\,8$ then $x$ is even, and if $x$ is even then $x\,|\,8.$

III. $x\,|\,8$ if and only if $x$ is even.
q-171781.worked_solution:
A biconditional expression $P⇔Q≡(P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P)$ can be read as shown below:

- $P$ if and only if $Q$

- $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

- If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A⇔B$ translates into the following sentences:

- $x\,|\,8$ if and only if $x$ is even.

- $x\,|\,8$ is equivalent to $x$ is even.

- If $x\,|\,8$ then $x$ is even, and if $x$ is even then $x\,|\,8.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
